 Mike Tomlin revisits Myles Garrett and Steelers’ Mason Rudolph incident with wild remark
 Steelers former coach Mike Tomlin jokes about Mason Rudolph while revisiting the Myles Garrett helmet incident and the infamous rivalry.
 By Clark Garret Alvarez • Updated Nov 13, 2026 at 1:03 AM ET • 2 min read Add ClutchPoints on Google Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Former Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike Tomlin revisited one of the NFL's most infamous altercations with an unexpected joke about Mason Rudolph . Years after the quarterback's confrontation with Myles Garrett , Tomlin offered a surprisingly humorous perspective on the incident.
 The former Steelers coach previously refused to revisit the Garrett-Rudolph controversy. However, his latest comments suggest he can now laugh about what happened.
 During an appearance on Cameron Heyward's Not Just Football podcast, Tomlin joked about Rudolph's appearance while discussing the notorious 2019 confrontation.
 Andrew Fillipponi shared Tomlin's remarks about Rudolph on X, highlighting the coach's unusual description of his former quarterback.
 “He's our punchable face,” Tomlin joked. “He kind of lightened the mood, though, when I said it, right? I was like, yeah, he does. He is very punchable.”
 The comments referenced the November 14, 2019, matchup between Pittsburgh and Cleveland. Garrett ripped off Rudolph's helmet and struck him with it during the closing seconds of the Browns' 21-7 victory.
 The incident triggered a larger confrontation involving several players. The NFL subsequently suspended Garrett for the remainder of the regular season and any Cleveland postseason games.
 At the time, Tomlin publicly defended Rudolph amid the controversy. The Steelers also stood behind their quarterback following the confrontation, with Heyward among those supporting him.
 Tomlin's latest remarks mark a striking change in tone from his earlier responses. What once generated intense controversy has now become the subject of an unexpected joke.
 Still, the helmet incident remains one of the defining moments in the Steelers-Browns rivalry even years later.
